description: Keymind Cascade MeshCore v1.17.1.1 infrastructure firmware plus corrected v1.17.1.2 Companion firmware, with Halo/Keymind retry tuning, Cascade defaults, and the USA/Canada 910.525 MHz / SF7 / BW62.5 / CR5 preset. Companion device power saving is enabled by default and migrated on once in the corrected release. Logging profiles are intended for a USB-connected MQTT/logging host. Unaffected roles remain on v1.17.1.1.

companionWifi.name: Companion WiFi
companionWifi.description: Companion radio over trusted local Wi-Fi (TCP port 5000). First-time network setup uses the MeshCore setup access point; this custom role may not map to the standard Configure step.

sensor.name: Sensor
sensor.description: Telemetry node that reads and publishes only the sensors compiled for and detected on the selected board; this custom role is not a companion or repeater.

terminalChat.name: Terminal Chat
terminalChat.description: Standalone text-chat client operated from a serial terminal; it does not expose the normal companion-app interface and may not map to the standard Configure step.

companionEthernet.name: Companion Ethernet
companionEthernet.description: Companion radio over wired Ethernet (TCP port 5000). Requires compatible Ethernet hardware and a DHCP network; this custom role may not map to the standard Configure step.

usb-packet-logging-v1.17.1.2-c9652754.notes:
Keymind Cascade MeshCore v1.17.1.2 with Halo/Keymind retry tuning, Cascade defaults, and the USA/Canada 910.525 MHz / SF7 / BW62.5 / CR5 preset.

ROLE — Companion USB: bridges a computer or host app to LoRa over USB serial. Choose it for a wired companion connection, not for an unattended repeater.

PROFILE — USB packet logging: keeps the selected role/profile, turns USB debug and packet logging ON. Host-side software can consume the serial stream and separately publish it to a computer-side MQTT broker. Expect substantial USB serial output; this build cannot install LoRa OTA unless the filename/profile explicitly says LoRa OTA.

INSTALL — First-time setup uses Full install (the merged bootloader + firmware image). Routine upgrades use Update (the app-only image) and normally preserve settings. Enable Erase all flash only when you intentionally want a clean reset.

POWER SAVING - v1.17.1.2 enables Companion device power saving by default. On first boot it migrates the saved Companion setting to on once, repairing devices that carried the regressed off value. A later explicit `powersaving off` choice remains persistent. This controls MCU/GPS idle saving and is separate from LoRa receive power saving (RXPS). On nRF52, an active USB data-host connection can intentionally keep the device awake; USB power from a charger alone does not.

LOGGING USE - This USB packet-logging build is for a USB-connected MQTT/logging host that reads the serial stream and publishes it. It is not the direct on-device Wi-Fi MQTT bridge.

full-usb-packet-logging-lora-ota-erase-r.notes:

REQUIRED FIRST FULL INSTALL — When installing FULL for the first time, or when moving from a non-FULL build, select Full install, use the merged .bin, and check Erase all flash before installing. The erase allows the expanded FULL partition table to replace the standard layout and deletes the node identity/private key, contacts, channels, and settings, so back up anything needed first. After the FULL layout is installed, later same-layout updates can use Update/app-only without erasing.

ROLE — Repeater: always-on infrastructure that relays mesh traffic. Configure its name/location, radio settings, and admin password. A repeater does not need an OTA-capable build merely to relay OTA traffic for other nodes.

LORA OTA — This page installs the base firmware, not a .mota package. Obtain and apply exact board-and-role .mota updates separately through the MeshCore LoRa OTA workflow; .mota files cannot be web flashed here.

SELECTION — FULL USB packet logging, LoRa OTA; first install erase required.

ROLE — Companion USB: bridges a computer or host app to LoRa over USB serial. Choose it for a wired companion connection, not for an unattended repeater.

PROFILE — USB packet logging: keeps the selected role/profile, turns USB debug and packet logging ON. Host-side software can consume the serial stream and separately publish it to a computer-side MQTT broker. Expect substantial USB serial output; this build cannot install LoRa OTA unless the filename/profile explicitly says LoRa OTA.

INSTALL — First-time setup uses Full install (the merged bootloader + firmware image). Routine upgrades use Update (the app-only image) and normally preserve settings. Enable Erase all flash only when you intentionally want a clean reset.

SELECTION — Serial.

POWER SAVING - v1.17.1.2 enables Companion device power saving by default. On first boot it migrates the saved Companion setting to on once, repairing devices that carried the regressed off value. A later explicit `powersaving off` choice remains persistent. This controls MCU/GPS idle saving and is separate from LoRa receive power saving (RXPS). On nRF52, an active USB data-host connection can intentionally keep the device awake; USB power from a charger alone does not.

LOGGING USE - This USB packet-logging build is for a USB-connected MQTT/logging host that reads the serial stream and publishes it. It is not the direct on-device Wi-Fi MQTT bridge.

full-usb-packet-logging-lora-ota-erase-r.notes:

REQUIRED FIRST FULL INSTALL — When installing FULL for the first time, or when moving from a non-FULL build, select Full install, use the merged .bin, and check Erase all flash before installing. The erase allows the expanded FULL partition table to replace the standard layout and deletes the node identity/private key, contacts, channels, and settings, so back up anything needed first. After the FULL layout is installed, later same-layout updates can use Update/app-only without erasing.

ROLE — ESP-NOW Repeater Bridge: relays normal MeshCore traffic and also bridges packets over ESP-NOW. Use it only for an ESP-NOW bridge/backhaul deployment; choose plain Repeater otherwise.

PROFILE — FULL USB packet logging + LoRa OTA: keeps the complete command/feature surface supported by this role and hardware, turns USB debug and packet logging ON, and turns LoRa OTA ON. Host-side software can consume the serial stream and separately publish it to a computer-side MQTT broker. Expect substantial USB serial output.

LORA OTA — This page installs the base firmware, not a .mota package. Obtain and apply exact board-and-role .mota updates separately through the MeshCore LoRa OTA workflow; .mota files cannot be web flashed here.

SELECTION — FULL USB packet logging, LoRa OTA; first install erase required.

REQUIRED FIRST FULL INSTALL — When installing FULL for the first time, or when moving from a non-FULL build, select Full install, use the merged .bin, and check Erase all flash before installing. The erase allows the expanded FULL partition table to replace the standard layout and deletes the node identity/private key, contacts, channels, and settings, so back up anything needed first. After the FULL layout is installed, later same-layout updates can use Update/app-only without erasing.

ROLE — Companion USB: bridges a computer or host app to LoRa over USB serial. Choose it for a wired companion connection, not for an unattended repeater.

PROFILE — USB packet logging: keeps the selected role/profile, turns USB debug and packet logging ON. Host-side software can consume the serial stream and separately publish it to a computer-side MQTT broker. Expect substantial USB serial output; this build cannot install LoRa OTA unless the filename/profile explicitly says LoRa OTA.

INSTALL — Browser flashing uses the Serial DFU .zip. The .uf2 is provided for manual drag-and-drop through a compatible UF2 bootloader volume. A normal firmware flash does not erase saved settings.

POWER SAVING - v1.17.1.2 enables Companion device power saving by default. On first boot it migrates the saved Companion setting to on once, repairing devices that carried the regressed off value. A later explicit `powersaving off` choice remains persistent. This controls MCU/GPS idle saving and is separate from LoRa receive power saving (RXPS). On nRF52, an active USB data-host connection can intentionally keep the device awake; USB power from a charger alone does not.

LOGGING USE - This USB packet-logging build is for a USB-connected MQTT/logging host that reads the serial stream and publishes it. It is not the direct on-device Wi-Fi MQTT bridge.

POWER SAVING - v1.17.1.2 enables Companion device power saving by default. On first boot it migrates the saved Companion setting to on once, repairing devices that carried the regressed off value. A later explicit `powersaving off` choice remains persistent. This controls MCU/GPS idle saving and is separate from LoRa receive power saving (RXPS). On nRF52, an active USB data-host connection can intentionally keep the device awake; USB power from a charger alone does not.

LOGGING USE - This USB packet-logging build is for a USB-connected MQTT/logging host that reads the serial stream and publishes it. It is not the direct on-device Wi-Fi MQTT bridge.

ROLE — Companion USB: bridges a computer or host app to LoRa over USB serial. Choose it for a wired companion connection, not for an unattended repeater.

PROFILE — USB packet logging: keeps the selected role/profile, turns USB debug and packet logging ON. Host-side software can consume the serial stream and separately publish it to a computer-side MQTT broker. Expect substantial USB serial output; this build cannot install LoRa OTA unless the filename/profile explicitly says LoRa OTA.

INSTALL — First-time setup uses Full install (the merged bootloader + firmware image). Routine upgrades use Update (the app-only image) and normally preserve settings. Enable Erase all flash only when you intentionally want a clean reset.

POWER SAVING - v1.17.1.2 enables Companion device power saving by default. On first boot it migrates the saved Companion setting to on once, repairing devices that carried the regressed off value. A later explicit `powersaving off` choice remains persistent. This controls MCU/GPS idle saving and is separate from LoRa receive power saving (RXPS). On nRF52, an active USB data-host connection can intentionally keep the device awake; USB power from a charger alone does not.

LOGGING USE - This USB packet-logging build is for a USB-connected MQTT/logging host that reads the serial stream and publishes it. It is not the direct on-device Wi-Fi MQTT bridge.

1w-pa-pins-dio1-1-nss-15-busy-38-usb-pac.notes:
Keymind Cascade MeshCore v1.17.1.2 with Halo/Keymind retry tuning, Cascade defaults, and the USA/Canada 910.525 MHz / SF7 / BW62.5 / CR5 preset.

ROLE — Companion USB: bridges a computer or host app to LoRa over USB serial. Choose it for a wired companion connection, not for an unattended repeater.

PROFILE — USB packet logging: keeps the selected role/profile, turns USB debug and packet logging ON. Host-side software can consume the serial stream and separately publish it to a computer-side MQTT broker. Expect substantial USB serial output; this build cannot install LoRa OTA unless the filename/profile explicitly says LoRa OTA.

INSTALL — First-time setup uses Full install (the merged bootloader + firmware image). Routine upgrades use Update (the app-only image) and normally preserve settings. Enable Erase all flash only when you intentionally want a clean reset.

SELECTION — 1W PA pins: DIO1 1, NSS 15, BUSY 38.

HARDWARE — Match the listed radio module, output stage, and pin map to the exact board; a similarly named radio variant is not a safe substitute.

Board selection note: Use this only for the LilyGo T-Beam 1W high-power PA board. It is not the standard T-Beam SX1262 target: this build uses LoRa DIO1=1, NSS=15, RESET=3, BUSY=38, SCLK/MISO/MOSI=13/12/11, RXEN=21, and GPS TX/RX=5/6. The standard T-Beam SX1262 target uses DIO1=33, NSS=18, RESET=23, SCLK/MISO/MOSI=5/19/27, and GPS RX/TX=12/34.

POWER SAVING - v1.17.1.2 enables Companion device power saving by default. On first boot it migrates the saved Companion setting to on once, repairing devices that carried the regressed off value. A later explicit `powersaving off` choice remains persistent. This controls MCU/GPS idle saving and is separate from LoRa receive power saving (RXPS). On nRF52, an active USB data-host connection can intentionally keep the device awake; USB power from a charger alone does not.

LOGGING USE - This USB packet-logging build is for a USB-connected MQTT/logging host that reads the serial stream and publishes it. It is not the direct on-device Wi-Fi MQTT bridge.

full-usb-packet-logging-lora-ota-erase-r.notes:
Keymind Cascade MeshCore v1.17.1.1 with Halo/Keymind retry tuning, Cascade defaults, and the USA/Canada 910.525 MHz / SF7 / BW62.5 / CR5 preset.

REQUIRED FIRST FULL INSTALL — When installing FULL for the first time, or when moving from a non-FULL build, select Full install, use the merged .bin, and check Erase all flash before installing. The erase allows the expanded FULL partition table to replace the standard layout and deletes the node identity/private key, contacts, channels, and settings, so back up anything needed first. After the FULL layout is installed, later same-layout updates can use Update/app-only without erasing.

ROLE — Room Server: hosts a MeshCore room and its message service. Configure the room identity/password and administrator credentials; choose Repeater when only packet forwarding is needed.

PROFILE — FULL USB packet logging + LoRa OTA: keeps the complete command/feature surface supported by this role and hardware, turns USB debug and packet logging ON, and turns LoRa OTA ON. Host-side software can consume the serial stream and separately publish it to a computer-side MQTT broker. Expect substantial USB serial output.

LORA OTA — This page installs the base firmware, not a .mota package. Obtain and apply exact board-and-role .mota updates separately through the MeshCore LoRa OTA workflow; .mota files cannot be web flashed here.

SELECTION — FULL USB packet logging, LoRa OTA; first install erase required.

mqtt-observer-v1.17.1.1-759a35fc.notes:
Keymind Cascade MeshCore v1.17.1.1 with Halo/Keymind retry tuning, Cascade defaults, and the USA/Canada 910.525 MHz / SF7 / BW62.5 / CR5 preset.

ROLE — Room Server: hosts a MeshCore room and its message service. Configure the room identity/password and administrator credentials; choose Repeater when only packet forwarding is needed.

PROFILE — Portable on-device MQTT observer: publishes observed mesh traffic directly from the device to a configured MQTT broker over Wi-Fi, keeps USB debug/packet logging OFF, uses a reduced admin CLI to fit the standard ESP32 app slot, and cannot install LoRa OTA.

INSTALL — First-time setup uses Full install (the merged bootloader + firmware image). Routine upgrades use Update (the app-only image) and normally preserve settings. Enable Erase all flash only when you intentionally want a clean reset.

SELECTION — Observer MQTT.

standard-v1.17.1.1-759a35fc.notes:
Keymind Cascade MeshCore v1.17.1.1 with Halo/Keymind retry tuning, Cascade defaults, and the USA/Canada 910.525 MHz / SF7 / BW62.5 / CR5 preset.

ROLE — Terminal Chat: standalone text chat operated from a serial terminal. It does not expose the standard companion-app interface, and this custom role may not show the standard Configure step.

PROFILE — Standard/utility: normal features for the selected role and hardware, with USB debug/packet logging and LoRa self-update OFF.

INSTALL — First-time setup uses Full install (the merged bootloader + firmware image). Routine upgrades use Update (the app-only image) and normally preserve settings. Enable Erase all flash only when you intentionally want a clean reset.

SELECTION — Serial terminal chat.

usb-packet-logging-v1.17.1.2-c9652754.notes:
Keymind Cascade MeshCore v1.17.1.2 with Halo/Keymind retry tuning, Cascade defaults, and the USA/Canada 910.525 MHz / SF7 / BW62.5 / CR5 preset.

ROLE — Companion USB: bridges a computer or host app to LoRa over USB serial. Choose it for a wired companion connection, not for an unattended repeater.

PROFILE — USB packet logging: keeps the selected role/profile, turns USB debug and packet logging ON. Host-side software can consume the serial stream and separately publish it to a computer-side MQTT broker. Expect substantial USB serial output; this build cannot install LoRa OTA unless the filename/profile explicitly says LoRa OTA.

INSTALL — First-time setup uses Full install (the merged bootloader + firmware image). Routine upgrades use Update (the app-only image) and normally preserve settings. Enable Erase all flash only when you intentionally want a clean reset.

POWER SAVING - v1.17.1.2 enables Companion device power saving by default. On first boot it migrates the saved Companion setting to on once, repairing devices that carried the regressed off value. A later explicit `powersaving off` choice remains persistent. This controls MCU/GPS idle saving and is separate from LoRa receive power saving (RXPS). On nRF52, an active USB data-host connection can intentionally keep the device awake; USB power from a charger alone does not.

LOGGING USE - This USB packet-logging build is for a USB-connected MQTT/logging host that reads the serial stream and publishes it. It is not the direct on-device Wi-Fi MQTT bridge.

usb-packet-logging-v1.17.1.2-c9652754.notes:
Keymind Cascade MeshCore v1.17.1.2 with Halo/Keymind retry tuning, Cascade defaults, and the USA/Canada 910.525 MHz / SF7 / BW62.5 / CR5 preset.

ROLE — Companion USB: bridges a computer or host app to LoRa over USB serial. Choose it for a wired companion connection, not for an unattended repeater.

PROFILE — USB packet logging: keeps the selected role/profile, turns USB debug and packet logging ON. Host-side software can consume the serial stream and separately publish it to a computer-side MQTT broker. Expect substantial USB serial output; this build cannot install LoRa OTA unless the filename/profile explicitly says LoRa OTA.

INSTALL — Browser flashing uses the Serial DFU .zip. The .uf2 is provided for manual drag-and-drop through a compatible UF2 bootloader volume. A normal firmware flash does not erase saved settings.

POWER SAVING - v1.17.1.2 enables Companion device power saving by default. On first boot it migrates the saved Companion setting to on once, repairing devices that carried the regressed off value. A later explicit `powersaving off` choice remains persistent. This controls MCU/GPS idle saving and is separate from LoRa receive power saving (RXPS). On nRF52, an active USB data-host connection can intentionally keep the device awake; USB power from a charger alone does not.

LOGGING USE - This USB packet-logging build is for a USB-connected MQTT/logging host that reads the serial stream and publishes it. It is not the direct on-device Wi-Fi MQTT bridge.

full-usb-packet-logging-lora-ota-erase-r.notes:
Keymind Cascade MeshCore v1.17.1.1 with Halo/Keymind retry tuning, Cascade defaults, and the USA/Canada 910.525 MHz / SF7 / BW62.5 / CR5 preset.

REQUIRED FIRST FULL INSTALL — When installing FULL for the first time, or when moving from a non-FULL build, select Full install, use the merged .bin, and check Erase all flash before installing. The erase allows the expanded FULL partition table to replace the standard layout and deletes the node identity/private key, contacts, channels, and settings, so back up anything needed first. After the FULL layout is installed, later same-layout updates can use Update/app-only without erasing.

ROLE — Sensor: publishes telemetry from sensors compiled for and detected on this board. It is not a general companion or repeater, and unsupported external sensors will not become available by flashing it.

PROFILE — FULL USB packet logging + LoRa OTA: keeps the complete command/feature surface supported by this role and hardware, turns USB debug and packet logging ON, and turns LoRa OTA ON. SELECTION — Sensor telemetry node, FULL USB packet logging, LoRa OTA; first install erase required.

usb-packet-logging-v1.17.1.2-c9652754.notes:
Keymind Cascade MeshCore v1.17.1.2 with Halo/Keymind retry tuning, Cascade defaults, and the USA/Canada 910.525 MHz / SF7 / BW62.5 / CR5 preset.

ROLE — Companion USB: bridges a computer or host app to LoRa over USB serial. Choose it for a wired companion connection, not for an unattended repeater.

PROFILE — USB packet logging: keeps the selected role/profile, turns USB debug and packet logging ON. Host-side software can consume the serial stream and separately publish it to a computer-side MQTT broker. Expect substantial USB serial output; this build cannot install LoRa OTA unless the filename/profile explicitly says LoRa OTA.

INSTALL — Browser flashing uses the Serial DFU .zip. The .uf2 is provided for manual drag-and-drop through a compatible UF2 bootloader volume. A normal firmware flash does not erase saved settings.

POWER SAVING - v1.17.1.2 enables Companion device power saving by default. On first boot it migrates the saved Companion setting to on once, repairing devices that carried the regressed off value. A later explicit `powersaving off` choice remains persistent. This controls MCU/GPS idle saving and is separate from LoRa receive power saving (RXPS). On nRF52, an active USB data-host connection can intentionally keep the device awake; USB power from a charger alone does not.

LOGGING USE - This USB packet-logging build is for a USB-connected MQTT/logging host that reads the serial stream and publishes it. It is not the direct on-device Wi-Fi MQTT bridge.

ROLE — Companion USB: bridges a computer or host app to LoRa over USB serial. Choose it for a wired companion connection, not for an unattended repeater.

PROFILE — USB packet logging: keeps the selected role/profile, turns USB debug and packet logging ON. Host-side software can consume the serial stream and separately publish it to a computer-side MQTT broker. Expect substantial USB serial output; this build cannot install LoRa OTA unless the filename/profile explicitly says LoRa OTA.

INSTALL — Browser flashing uses the Serial DFU .zip. The .uf2 is provided for manual drag-and-drop through a compatible UF2 bootloader volume. A normal firmware flash does not erase saved settings.

SELECTION — 30S, SX1262 22 dBm.

HARDWARE — Match the listed radio module, output stage, and pin map to the exact board; a similarly named radio variant is not a safe substitute.

POWER SAVING - v1.17.1.2 enables Companion device power saving by default. On first boot it migrates the saved Companion setting to on once, repairing devices that carried the regressed off value. A later explicit `powersaving off` choice remains persistent. This controls MCU/GPS idle saving and is separate from LoRa receive power saving (RXPS). On nRF52, an active USB data-host connection can intentionally keep the device awake; USB power from a charger alone does not.

LOGGING USE - This USB packet-logging build is for a USB-connected MQTT/logging host that reads the serial stream and publishes it. It is not the direct on-device Wi-Fi MQTT bridge.

ROLE — Repeater: always-on infrastructure that relays mesh traffic. Configure its name/location, radio settings, and admin password. A repeater does not need an OTA-capable build merely to relay OTA traffic for other nodes.

PROFILE — USB packet logging: keeps the selected role/profile, turns USB debug and packet logging ON. Host-side software can consume the serial stream and separately publish it to a computer-side MQTT broker. Expect substantial USB serial output; this build cannot install LoRa OTA unless the filename/profile explicitly says LoRa OTA.

INSTALL — Browser flashing uses the Serial DFU .zip. The .uf2 is provided for manual drag-and-drop through a compatible UF2 bootloader volume. A normal firmware flash does not erase saved settings.

usb-packet-logging-v1.17.1.2-c9652754.notes:
Keymind Cascade MeshCore v1.17.1.2 with Halo/Keymind retry tuning, Cascade defaults, and the USA/Canada 910.525 MHz / SF7 / BW62.5 / CR5 preset.

ROLE — Companion USB: bridges a computer or host app to LoRa over USB serial. Choose it for a wired companion connection, not for an unattended repeater.

PROFILE — USB packet logging: keeps the selected role/profile, turns USB debug and packet logging ON. Host-side software can consume the serial stream and separately publish it to a computer-side MQTT broker. Expect substantial USB serial output; this build cannot install LoRa OTA unless the filename/profile explicitly says LoRa OTA.

INSTALL — First-time setup uses Full install (the merged bootloader + firmware image). Routine upgrades use Update (the app-only image) and normally preserve settings. Enable Erase all flash only when you intentionally want a clean reset.

POWER SAVING - v1.17.1.2 enables Companion device power saving by default. On first boot it migrates the saved Companion setting to on once, repairing devices that carried the regressed off value. A later explicit `powersaving off` choice remains persistent. This controls MCU/GPS idle saving and is separate from LoRa receive power saving (RXPS). On nRF52, an active USB data-host connection can intentionally keep the device awake; USB power from a charger alone does not.

LOGGING USE - This USB packet-logging build is for a USB-connected MQTT/logging host that reads the serial stream and publishes it. It is not the direct on-device Wi-Fi MQTT bridge.

full-usb-packet-logging-lora-ota-erase-r.notes:
Keymind Cascade MeshCore v1.17.1.1 with Halo/Keymind retry tuning, Cascade defaults, and the USA/Canada 910.525 MHz / SF7 / BW62.5 / CR5 preset.

REQUIRED FIRST FULL INSTALL — When installing FULL for the first time, or when moving from a non-FULL build, select Full install, use the merged .bin, and check Erase all flash before installing. The erase allows the expanded FULL partition table to replace the standard layout and deletes the node identity/private key, contacts, channels, and settings, so back up anything needed first. After the FULL layout is installed, later same-layout updates can use Update/app-only without erasing.

LORA OTA — This page installs the base firmware, not a .mota package. Obtain and apply exact board-and-role .mota updates separately through the MeshCore LoRa OTA workflow; .mota files cannot be web flashed here.

SELECTION — FULL USB packet logging, LoRa OTA; first install erase required.
